title: Sharp modulus range for triangle counts in dense random graphs

initial.assessment: Exact TeX and all five native pages read; reconstructed chaos variance, finite-window summability, mesh normal variation, and necessary Fourier frequency subsequence.

proof: Graphwise expansion in centered edge indicators has orthogonal terms since an edge appears once in the symmetric difference. Exact variance and equivalent covariance form give σ_n asymptotic to a positive constant times n². The ordinary count is used throughout.

Bounded differences with N coordinate ranges n−2 gives exponential full tail at B√log n standard deviations. Central points per progression are at most 2Bσ/q+1, so relative local-limit error is δ_n(2B+q/σ). Full tails absorb q≤σ, and absolute Gaussian mesh discrepancy is at most √(2/π)q/σ, uniformly in residue and phase. This includes slowly vanishing, bounded and composite modulus sequences.

First modular Fourier coefficient is bounded by the relative maximum discrepancy when q≥2. On a subsequence q/σ≥c, varying Gaussian-characteristic frequencies converge after further subsequence; bounded first absolute centered moment controls the difference, so the limit magnitude is nonzero. The stated edge CLT uses a residual with vanishing normalized variance. Density-to-unit-cell Taylor integration gives the correct 1/24 coefficient and error order.
primary: Actual Theorem1.1 ordinary connected graph count, G(n,p), true variance and rate n^{−1/2+ε} after multiplying σ. Deep local theorem is a credited published import, not fully reproved.
Actual Scott/Tateno pp1279–1280 already identify necessary scale, announce sufficient q=o(n²/log n) for integer moduli, and give the Gaussian cell convention.

Actual Gilmer–Kopparty Lemmas4–5 and subsequent global characteristic bound. Modular Fourier inversion and pairing j/q with (q−j)/q give bound O((q/σ)^{1+δ}), confirming the honest earlier sufficient consequence.
